name: 3S Map (GMCP)
author: Joakim
description: The automapper, rebuilt on GMCP: rooms identified by the number the server gives them rather than by dead reckoning, so position is never inferred and so never drifts. Links are room number to room number, learned from what the server states and from what you actually walk; where the two disagree it says so and believes the walk - unless the exit is marked SHIFTING (an elevator, a portal: 'mapg shift', or automatic after walking it to two different places), in which case nothing is learned or routed through it, you ride it yourself, and the map is cut on both sides of it - each elevator floor its own map, the car a map of its own. Draws one grid per area, and one more for each unconnected piece of an area - so 'Unknown', which labels every stretch of connective realm on the MUD rather than one place, becomes a handful of readable maps instead of one tangle. Coordinates are a layout recomputed from the links, never an identity. Walks routes on request, one confirmed step at a time: the next step goes out only when the server says we reached the room the route expected, and anything unexpected stops it. Explores on request (folded in from the lab's 3s-map-explorer at 1.8.0): 'mapg explore area [N]' sweeps the area you stand in and 'mapg explore all' the whole world, a route to the nearest room with an unexplored exit, then one step through it, then again - one move per confirmed arrival, exactly as a requested walk moves. An exit is unexplored when the room behind it is not in the store. Everything that stops a walk stops the sweep - a combat round starting (it reads Char.Combat for this), a move you typed, the watchdog, 'mapg stop', an HP floor ('mapg explore hp') - and nothing here ever resumes on its own. A probe that does not land marks that exit blocked for the session and the sweep goes on; a fenced sweep that lands in another area steps straight back and remembers the door as an edge; a budget N stops after N new rooms; every end prints and puts on the panel the same summary. Everything it ever sends is a single bare word from the move/door vocabulary. The panel: the map with a colour legend, doors to other maps drawn in their direction, Explore beside Stop and the sweep's live line; the Maps and Favs tabs; right-click a room, or a row, for a menu of typed mapg commands - walk there, the route, the room, forget it - and right-click your own square to mark an exit shifting. 'mapg forget map|area' drops a whole map or area, asking first like 'mapg wipe'. Overlays (1.9.0): Room.Map's line-of-sight grid paints the rooms the server shows monsters or players in; a route lights the rooms it runs through - the walk's own, a 'Show route' you asked for (until you move, or 'mapg stop'), or the farmer's next leg as it patrols; and the farmer's rest room is drawn beside its other rules. Click any room (1.10.0) for a details line under the map - name, exits, how often you stood there, what Room.Contents last showed there - with links that walk, light the route or print the room; and Places: 'mapg place <name>' bookmarks a room, 'mapg go <name>' walks to it, the Places tab lists them (click walks, right-click removes), the map marks them. 'mapg find <text>' (1.11.0) lights every room named like it and lists them on the Find tab, which also carries the Doors table - every way off the map you stand on, a click walks through. The only mapper Scrye ships since 1.8.0; the dead-reckoning 3s-map it ran beside is retired. 1.11.1 (23 Sep): a learned link in a direction the room's exit list does not name is dropped; the details line reads a crowded room's paged Room.Contents whole and counts a monster's count.
